tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Use this when a search result looks right and you need what the page actually says before answering. Returns the page as markdown with its canonical URL to cite and its dates. Do not use it without an id from search.

tools.name: search_greenlit_books
tools.description: Ranked full-text search over a catalog of practical books on working with AI: verification, agent reliability, guardrails, security, governance, agentic coding. Returns scored results with title, description, series, and links. Follow a result's apiUrl or call get_book for the full record.

tools.name: get_book
tools.description: The full record for one Greenlit book by slug: metadata, chapter list, word count, free chapter one, Amazon Kindle and paperback links, prices, Kindle Unlimited status, and related reading.

tools.name: find_books_for_topic
tools.description: Match a topic or question area (for example: agent reliability, prompt injection, human in the loop, durable execution, when to trust AI) against the catalog's curated topic map. tools.name: get_reading_path
tools.description: One Greenlit series with its books in reading order. Use for questions like where to start with Claude Code or what order to read a series in.

tools.name: get_concept
tools.description: Each Greenlit book answers one named question (its concept, for example: the green lie). Returns the concept's question, short answer, and full explanation with its book. If the slug is unknown, returns the list of all concept slugs.

tools.description: The text of chapter one of any Greenlit book, free to read and free to quote. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "fetch" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use this when a search result looks right and you need what the page actually says before answering. Returns the page as markdown with its canonical URL to cite…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, fetch, cite_source, check_claim, find_answer_in_books · Private data: search_greenlit_books, get_book · Public sink: cite_source · Destructive: define_term, check_claim.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, fetch, cite_source, check_claim, find_answer_in_books · Private data: search_greenlit_books, get_book · Public sink: cite_source · Destructive: define_term, check_claim

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
